**No, `--binary-files=binary` is rejected.** The parser returns a usage error for it (src/main.zig:3186-3187), with a message containing "never prints binary content" (src/main.zig:3189). The reason given: in grep, `binary` means "print matches but suppress binary content", which this engine can't do, so it is rejected at parse time rather than silently accepted (src/main.zig:240-242).

The only accepted values are `text` and `without_match` (src/main.zig:243):

- **`text`**: hunts the file and prints the matches (src/main.zig:239-240). It is equivalent to `-a` (src/main.zig:330). A test confirms `--binary-files=text` parses (src/main.zig:3180-3182).
- **`without-match`**: pretends the binary file does not match (src/main.zig:240-241). It is the default (src/main.zig:331, 330).

The context doesn't show the actual string parsing, so I can't confirm whether the hyphenated spelling `without-match` is what the parser accepts. The enum field is `without_match`, and the comment at src/main.zig:330 uses the hyphenated form.
